Thanks Elena — great meeting. I'm attaching a proposed MAP that separates technical evaluation milestones from legal/procurement gates so your stakeholders can parallel-track where sensible. Quick summary of the proposed critical path:

- Week 0 (kickoff): mutual action plan signed by both PMs (non‑binding) and technical kickoff
- Tech eval (2 weeks): integration, latency/cost benchmarks, acceptance prompt set results
- Security evidence handoff (by Week 2): SOC 2 report, retention policy, audit-log sample
- Legal close (Week 3–4): MSA redlines + DPA sign, then order form signature to activate reserved pilot capacity

If procurement needs hard dates, I can shift the plan but recommend DPA and SOC2 be completed before signing the order form.

I've attached: MAP_v1_BioTex.xlsx (delineated milestones), a draft order form, and MSA redlines for Laura to review.

Action items for Redwood:
- Laura: review MSA redlines and indicate must‑haves vs negotiables
- Priyom: confirm if we can provide a limited audit-log extract for their security team by 3/24
- Kimberly: price impact if we need an interim SLA for pilot (short-term credit/discount)

Will follow up with a short call invite with procurement to align on dates.

Marcus / Elena — quick legal read. High level:

1) MSA redlines v3 — I annotated three required items we can't accept to be excised: (a) open-ended indemnity for customer subcontractors, (b) deletion of our standard liability cap tied to fees, and (c) an overly broad data-scanning clause.

2) DPA — we can sign the standard DPA once we confirm processing activities and subprocessor list. Need BioTex to confirm any additional retention or special category data.

3) Order form gating — recommend: order form executes last to ensure MSA+DPA are final. If procurement requires parallel signature for commercial timing, we'd accept an executed order form contingent on legal holdback language (one‑page clause).

I added marginal comments in MSA_redlines_v3.pdf. Laura

Folks — security/ops notes:

- SOC 2: we can provide our latest Type II report (Q4 2026). I'll pull the attestation and a short narrative of controls mapped to their review checklist by 3/22.
- Audit logs: we can provide a sampled export (anonymized) covering the pilot workspace for the week of the integration; format will be CSV with event type, timestamp, and request id.
- Retention policy: our default is 90 days for KV cache artifacts and 365 days for logs; we can propose 180 days if that helps their compliance team.

If BioTex needs an HSM/KMS integration or on‑prem option, that will push the timeline — call that out in the MAP as an alternate path.
